Ability Scores - Method V (4d6, drop lowest)
Click the dice to roll. Drag one score onto another to swap them.

Before you choose a people or a profession, the dice reveal the raw material of the hero you will become. In AD&D 2nd Edition, six ability scores govern almost every challenge: opening doors, dodging dragon breath, resisting poison, learning spells, sensing lies, and leading companions.\r\rThis wizard uses Method V from the Player's Handbook: roll 4d6 for each ability, drop the lowest die, then assign the six results where you will. Drag one score onto another to swap them until the array suits your vision.\r\rStrength measures muscle and brawn. It sets melee damage, the weight you can carry, and chances to bend bars or force doors. Fighters, paladins, and rangers with 18 Strength may roll percentile dice (01-00) for exceptional Strength (18/xx); use the second dice icon beside Strength when it appears.\r\rDexterity is quickness and aim: Armor Class, missile attacks, and reactions in surprise. Constitution is hardiness: hit points per level, system shock, resurrection survival, and poison saves. Intelligence governs languages, arcane spellcraft, and how readily you learn. Wisdom supports priestly magic, magical defense, and insight. Charisma shapes loyalty, henchmen, and reaction rolls.\r\rWrite no score in stone too soon. Race and class choices on the following tabs may raise or lower these numbers, and some kits demand minimum scores. Roll honestly, arrange with care, then step forward into the Realms.
